page: Microsoft Azure B8ps_v2 is an ARM64-based virtual machine within Azure's burstable general-purpose series, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz, configured with 8 vCPUs mapped directly to 8 physical cores with 1 thread per core. Memory allocation totals 32.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The CPU subsystem includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware acceleration for AES cryptographic operations while lacking AVX and AMX vector extensions.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating network-attached Azure Premium Storage for persistent file access and operating system volumes. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the B8ps_v2 yields mid-tier multi-threaded throughput, posting 14,508.5 in multi-core stress-ng tests, 6,099.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 11.04 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth registers at 88.51 GB/s for uncached large-block reads and 47.79 GB/s for writes. Conversely, single-threaded performance is lower, exhibiting bottom-tier results in Geekbench single-core at 1,105.0 and PassMark CPU scoring at 6,250.19.

Because CPU capacity operates under a burstable credit model, continuous sustained computational loads may exhaust credits and degrade processing velocity. The platform delivers strong resource economy for applications with variable activity profiles by leveraging cost-efficient ARM silicon. The instance provides an effective foundation for static web serving, software build pipelines, staging environments, intermediate caching, and microservices where baseline CPU consumption remains modest with occasional compute spikes.
description: Microsoft Azure B8ps_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine powered by an 8-core Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Equipped with 32 GB of system memory, it maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per physical core, with no simultaneous multithreading. The instance features no local disk storage, relying on external Premium Storage integration, and does not include dedicated graphics processing units. In benchmark evaluations, the B8ps_v2 demonstrates balanced multi-core throughput, recording 14,508.5 in stress-ng multi-core testing, 6,099.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 10.75 GB/s in static web serving. However, single-core metrics remain modest, reflected in bottom-quartile Geekbench and PassMark single-thread and encryption scores. Delivering cost efficiency via burstable CPU scheduling and ARM architecture efficiency, the B8ps_v2 fits development environments, microservices, code compilation, and web workloads with intermittent processing demands.
